A1.justification: Both readable 19-page PDFs describe FUMO, with corresponding methods, equations, experiments, figures, and tables. Full-file inspection found no appendices in either supplied PDF.

before.justification: v1 reports original reflection-removal experiments on Nature, Real, and SIR2, qualitative examples, and component ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 4–7.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a concatenation ablation, reflection-localization accuracy, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The dual-prior extraction, ControlNet gate, one-step diffusion, refinement module, and training losses remain unchanged. The corrected gated-condition symbol at inference in Section 3.3 aligns with the modulation procedure already described in v1.

E1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an auxiliary reflection-region localization evaluation on annotated real images. Its image source is unspecified. The restoration training datasets, Nature/Real/SIR2 benchmarks, and in-the-wild coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 2 add Concat, which concatenates both priors with the ControlNet condition, as a comparator to gated modulation. The seven external baselines in Table 1 and all previous ablation variants are retained.

E3.justification: The new grounding evaluation specifies 100 annotated images and mIoU. New efficiency measurements use 1K resolution on one RTX 4090. The concatenation experiment adds a conditioning control; existing training schedules, restoration splits, preprocessing, and quality metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The added Concat ablation tests whether residual modulation outperforms direct prior concatenation. Section 3.1 also adds a diagnostic assessment of the grounding component's localization accuracy. Existing gate and refinement analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 and existing Table 2 entries are unchanged. The new Concat column reports PSNR 26.87, SSIM 0.906, LPIPS 0.072, CLIPIQA 0.406, and MUSIQ 58.55. v2 also reports grounding mIoU of 0.65 and new runtime/resource measurements.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 retain the same definitions and objectives. The inference-conditioning notation correction introduces no new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim dual-prior guidance, coarse-to-fine diffusion restoration, and competitive quantitative performance with improved perceptual quality. Replacing controllability wording with spatial adaptivity and tightening the contribution bullets preserves these claims' substantive scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations concerning overlapping layers with similar intensity and structure, and VLM inference overhead, with proposed mitigation directions. Section 4.3 adds the interpretation that modulation uses the priors more effectively than direct concatenation.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly reports 3.40 s for prior extraction and 0.63 s for restoration at 1K on one RTX 4090, plus 1.72B parameters, 1512.96G FLOPs, and 4.96GB peak memory. Existing optimization settings and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds twelve cited works, including DPM-Solver++, LightenDiffusion, and HazeCLIP, and briefly expands discussion of image/video enhancement and VLM guidance. The central positioning within prior-guided reflection removal remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 tightens the abstract, contribution bullets, and method explanations; standardizes terminology and grammar; and adds limitations and acknowledgements. Affiliation and bibliography text are updated, while the main section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes the intensity-prior color rendering and adjusts image crops. Table 2 gains a Concat column with tighter spacing. Minor caption edits and page reflow accompany these changes; the overall figure and table organization is retained.

improvement.justification: The added Concat comparison directly strengthens evidence for gated modulation. Grounding accuracy, computational measurements, and explicit failure conditions improve validation and transparency. Main benchmark results remain unchanged, and the grounding evaluation is only briefly documented, so the overall gains are useful but limited.
